assumptions: A qualified assessor or integrator would retain all conformity judgments and related liability, while the product remains limited to evidence ingestion and version-bound release records.
One selected PLC or robot-cell stack exposes sufficiently consistent export artefacts, and machine owners permit the required secure access, for mappings to be reused across projects.
The proposed provenance workflow is not already adequately handled by the target partner's CE, PLM, engineering, or incumbent compliance tools.
The stated channel pricing, activation volume, and gross-margin ranges are planning hypotheses rather than validated commercial results.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid design-partner commitment from a qualified high-volume integrator or assessor, a workflow audit proving the version-provenance gap is not covered by incumbent tools, and a live single-stack pilot showing measurable reconciliation savings, secure repeatable ingestion, acceptable liability boundaries, implementation hours, activation frequency, renewal intent, and contribution economics.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Narrowing from a broad CE workspace to a version-bound evidence connector identifies a specific handover control point and respects the boundary between data provenance and qualified safety judgment. However, the central claim that this control point is materially uncovered remains explicitly unknown.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Regulatory documentation duties and incumbent compliance spending establish a real budget category, but the packet provides no measured handover failure frequency, labor cost, customer interviews, paid pilot, or evidence that partners will fund this separate connector. Existing software and consultancies may already satisfy the need.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual white-label licensing plus per-machine activation could create recurring, usage-linked revenue with low initial capital needs. Yet pricing, activation volume, 60-85% gross margins, payback, retention, and the 30-partner wealth path are all illustrative; bespoke mappings, support, security work, and long sales cycles could prevent software-like margins and owner earnings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single high-volume stack sold through qualified Polish assessors or integrators is appropriately narrow in concept. The actual machine category, stack, project volume, partner population, activation frequency, and economically meaningful beachhead size have not been identified.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Embedding white-label inside an established partner workflow could produce a focused position, but mature CE platforms already provide documentation, change tracking, traceability, collaboration, and expert support. The packet does not show that the connector owns a gap incumbents, PLM tools, or integrators cannot readily add themselves.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful mapping and evidence schema could extend to additional machine releases, partners, PLC stacks, robot-cell categories, and geographies. Each adjacent stack may require new access, mappings, security approval, and domain work, so the repeatability of expansion is uncertain.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accumulated vendor-specific mappings and deep workflow integration could create modest switching costs and implementation know-how. No proprietary data rights, exclusive channel, network effect, certification moat, or hard-to-copy technology is established, and partners or incumbents may internalize the functionality.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Automatic linkage of exported program versions to release evidence could be faster and more reliable than manual reconciliation. The current evidence neither confirms the gap nor quantifies time savings, error reduction, compliance value, or superiority over incumbent and engineering-system workflows.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The Machinery Regulation's mandatory application in January 2027 creates near-term attention around documentation, software-related safety, and cyber-safety. The opportunity is moderated because substantial-modification duties are case-specific and established vendors and consultancies are already positioned for the transition.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A white-label assessor or integrator channel is logically aligned with existing engagements and reduces reliance on founder-led enterprise sales. No partner commitment, channel terms, CAC, sales-cycle evidence, or proof of scalable partner recruitment exists, and dependence on a few partners creates concentration and bargaining risk.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The data-lineage work fits the founder's technical strengths, the proposed pilot capital is manageable, and keeping safety judgments with qualified partners improves feasibility. Execution still depends on machinery-domain expertise, secure access to sensitive artefacts, reusable integrations, partner recruitment, liability boundaries, and sales cycles that may exceed part-time capacity.

highest_value_structural_change: Make one qualified high-volume integrator or assessor the paid anchor customer and deployment owner, narrow the product to that partner's one proven stack and export format, and require an annual-minimum plus per-release commitment tied to verified labor savings before building a generalized connector.
main_structural_strength: A tightly bounded, white-label provenance connector can sit inside an existing qualified partner's handover workflow, exploit the founder's data-lineage skills, and avoid assuming regulated safety judgments or building another full CE suite.
primary_score_limiter: The business depends simultaneously on an unverified incumbent product gap, a willing channel partner with secure artefact access, and sufficiently reusable single-stack mappings; none of those commercial prerequisites is evidenced.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Safexpert already advertises change tracking, traceable project histories, technical-documentation workflows, teamwork, and standards monitoring, while CEM4, CEDOC, and Pilz add lower-priced software and expert-led substitutes; this directly challenges the premise that a separate provenance layer is necessary and budgeted.
